title: Chicken & Egg Films Names 2026 R&D Grant Cohort Including Maite Alberdi, Sepideh Farsi & Sam Feder
summary: The Netflix-supported documentary program will distribute research and development funding to 30 filmmakers working across 26 projects.
body_markdown:
Chicken & Egg Films announced today the 26 film projects supported by its fourth


Chicken & Egg Films Research & Development Grant.


The grants provide filmmakers with $10,000 USD toward research or $20,000 USD toward the development of a new documentary project. These critical early stages in the life of a documentary often go unsupported. During their grant year, filmmakers will also have access to the Chicken & Egg Films team and community for peer support, expert mentorship, and industry connections. The 2026 Chicken & Egg Films Research & Development Grant is supported by Netflix. The Research & Development (R&D) Grant this year will be awarded to 30 filmmakers working on 26 projects. The cohort is 70% international – the most global to date. Together the 2026 R&D recipients represent 21 countries worldwide, including Argentina, Australia, Canada, Chile, China, France, Georgia, Germany, Guatemala, India, Iran, Kazakhstan, Lebanon, Madagascar, Mexico, Russia, South Korea, Spain, the UK, Ukraine, and the US. The R&D Grant recipients are divided into two segments. The Research Grant recipients are in the ideation period, which includes identifying secondary sources, following storylines, and building foundational relationships. The Development Grant recipients are in a deeper exploration period, which includes securing access to core subjects and collaborators, solidifying budgets, fundraising, story development and other tasks. “At a time when polarization and isolation can make the world feel smaller, these projects remind us that documentaries have the power to build connections across borders,” said Associate Director of Program Elaisha Stokes. “The stories we are supporting in this cohort reflect the world we hope to live in, one defined by curiosity, empathy, and new ways of understanding our shared humanity.” Every Chicken & Egg Films cohort offers a snapshot of the narratives, topics, and themes most urgent to filmmakers right now. This year's R&D slate is no exception, with stories exploring social issues spanning women's rights, climate, war, immigration, disability rights, democracy, and more. But despite this broad scope, the throughline across each film is intimacy: a father and daughter dig into what grief and memory pass down a bloodline; a filmmaker traces her family back through a colonial rupture that took forty-five years to come to light; a woman follows the ghost of her great-grandmother's execution straight into a war happening today. ABOUT CHICKEN & EGG FILMS


Chicken & Egg Films champions women and gender-expansive documentary filmmakers around the globe with funding, mentorship, and access so they can tell stories that ignite change. We match strategically-timed grants with creative guidance, peer community-building, and industry connections. This support system is tailored to meet the unique needs women and gender-expansive people experience in their filmmaking and career trajectories. As of 2026, we have provided over $15.5 million in grants and thousands of hours of creative mentorship to over 550 filmmakers from across the globe. Films supported by our work have been nationally and internationally recognized with critical accolades, including Academy Awards, Emmy Awards, and Peabody Awards. Recipient of honors including the Social Impact Media Awards Vanguard Award and the International Documentary Association’s Amicus Award, Chicken & Egg Films was first founded in 2005 to address the “chicken or egg” inequities women filmmakers faced. We’ve since evolved our eligibility criteria to support all filmmakers impacted by gender bias. For additional information, please visit chickeneggfilms.org.
